title: Smooth, short and held
summary: Hear and read slurs, staccato dots, accents and pauses, and tell a slur from a tie.
usSummary: Hear and read slurs, staccato dots, accents and fermatas, and tell a slur from a tie.

hook.text: Glide across a room and each step melts into the next. Now tiptoe: step, stop, step, stop. Press play: the same four notes are played twice. How is the second [[bar|bar]] different from the first? And what are those marks?

explore.text: Press play to hear four notes played two ways. Then find middle C on the keyboard and play C, D, E, F twice. First make them glide: hold each key until the next one starts. Then tiptoe: lift your finger straight away.
explore.goal: Play the clip, then play C D E F twice: joined up, then with a gap after each note.

cards.text: Smooth and joined, with no gaps, is [[legato|legato]]. A curved line over notes of different pitches, a [[slur|slur]], asks for it. Short and detached is [[staccato|staccato]]: a dot above or below each note. Listen to the first [[bar|bar]], then the second.

An [[accent|accent]] is a sideways V: lean on that note with extra force. A [[pause|pause]] is a dot under an arch: hold that note longer than written. Press play and listen for the accents, then the [[pause|pause]] at the end.

A slur and a [[tie|tie]] both curve. A tie joins two notes of the *same* pitch into one long sound. A slur joins *different* pitches, and each note is played. Two feeling words: [[cantabile|cantabile]] is in a singing style, [[dolce|dolce]] is sweet and soft.

alternative.text: Think of walking. Gliding is [[legato|legato]]: every step melts into the next. Tiptoeing is [[staccato|staccato]]. Stamping one foot is an [[accent|accent]]. A red light is a [[pause|pause]]: stop, wait, then go. Press play and follow the story.

questions.prompt: Match each sign to its name.

Dots above or below the notes ask for [[staccato|staccato]]: short and detached.
A sideways V is an [[accent|accent]]: play that note with extra force.

questions.hint: Two of these words are about touch. Two are about mood.

payload.explanation: [[bar|Bar]] 2 has staccato dots, but the clip plays it smoothly. It needs a slur, like the [[bar|bars]] on either side.

questions.prompt: Which sign tells you to hold a note longer than it is written?
questions.hint: It sits above the note like a small arch with a dot. Which of these is not a curve below the notes?

options.reason: A curve over notes is a [[slur|slur]]: it joins them smoothly but does not hold any of them longer. Holding is the arch with a dot, the [[pause|pause]].
A sideways V is an [[accent|accent]]: extra force on one note, not extra length. Holding is the arch with a dot, the [[pause|pause]].

points: A slur is a curved line over notes of different pitches: play them smoothly, as legato. Staccato is short and detached, with a dot above or below each note.
An accent is a sideways V: play that note with extra force. A [[pause|pause]] is a dot under an arch: hold the note longer than written.
A tie joins two notes of the same pitch into one long sound. A slur joins different pitches, and every note is played.
Cantabile means in a singing style, and dolce means sweet and soft.
